after_body:
Part of #19

Blocked by #23

## What to build

Build and compare two kinds of nonlinear task generators: structural causal mechanisms and a standalone random neural network. Include cases where either produces unusable tasks.

Expose controls for graph connections, sampled mechanisms, feature and target assignments, activation saturation and noise.

## What to save

Save a drawing of a sampled causal graph and its structural equations. Also show a standalone network with its feature and target assignments. Across seeds, report depth, output dispersion, unusable draws and rejection reasons.

## Done when

- Sampled mechanisms and their distributions can be inspected.
- Checks detect degenerate graphs, saturated outputs and target leakage.
- Each candidate has saved valid examples and rejection reasons.

## How to review it

Follow one causal example from its parent variables to its target using the saved noise draw. Inspect a slice of a network's response. Compare a saturated draw with an accepted draw. Show how filtering changes the variety of retained graphs or networks.

## Decisions still needed

Choose graph, activation, depth and sparsity families.

Original roadmap coverage: T17.


## Approved specification

[Authoritative accepted scope for #28](https://github.com/Avistian/r0/blob/66e91e243581c21dcde3975246d5f383678e9cec/docs/specs/0028-causal-network-generators.md). Implementation and verification must follow this specification.
